```jinja2
{%if '{' in option.value|string or '(' in option.value|string %}"{% endif %}-D{{option.macro_name}}={{option.value}}{% if '}' in option.value|string or ')' in option.value|string %}"{% endif %}
```

- option.value = "{\"mqtt.2030.ltsapis.goog\", IOTC_MQTT_PORT}"

1. Checks if '{' is in the value - YES, it is
2. Adds a quote at the beginning: `"-D{{option.macro_name}}={{option.value}}`
3. Checks if '}' is in the value - YES, it is

But this is wrong! The quote is placed BEFORE the -D, making it part of the string rather than properly enclosing the value.

The issue is that the quotes should enclose just the VALUE part, not the entire -D directive. Also, when the value itself contains quotes, those need to be properly escaped.

-DIOTC_MQTT_HOST="{\"mqtt.2030.ltsapis.goog\", IOTC_MQTT_PORT}"

-DIOTC_MQTT_HOST=\"{\"mqtt.2030.ltsapis.goog\", IOTC_MQTT_PORT}\"
